Maps with context

Historical maps

Explore authentic historical documents connected to this entry. Their names and boundaries reflect their makers and periods.

1837–1838 (archive date range) · Historical military-conflict context

Second Seminole War: Okefenokee region manuscript map

Greenleaf Dearborn (attributed by the archive)

The archive dates this military map to 1837–1838 during the Second Seminole War. It depicts forts and routes around the Okefenokee, providing historical context rather than Seminole-authored territorial information.

Historical scope: 1837–1838 (archive date range)

Evidence for this connection: UGA / Digital Library of Georgia: item record ↗

Map-room record & credits ↗Original archive ↗View both PDF pages ↗

Second Seminole War, Okefenokee region manuscript map, ms4209, Box1 Folder1, Hargrett Rare Book and Manuscript Library, University of Georgia Libraries; presented by the Digital Library of Georgia. No Copyright — United States ↗

[1902] · Named historical subject in archival guide

Creek & Seminole Nations, Indian Territory

C. H. Dana; U.S. Department of the Interior, Commission to the Five Civilized Tribes

The archive identifies the Creek and Seminole Nations as the map’s historical subjects. No current boundaries or particular modern government are inferred.

Historical scope: [1902]

Evidence for this connection: LOC guide: Creek and Seminole Nations, 1902 ↗
